person: Aisha Grant is a 31-year-old ED night nurse in Tucson, expecting her first baby next spring. She is moving from Tucson-area rentals to a possible house purchase with her partner, and noticed her address and phone on people-search sites after a credit report check. She sent a one-step deletion request through the state's platform in late August after moving from Arizona to California for a job stint, and wants to know what actually got removed. She was Aisha Okafor before marriage, so old listings sit under that name. She does admin in bursts on days off, from her phone.
stated_up_front: I sent one of those delete-my-data requests a while back and my info is still all over people-search sites. Can you check what actually happened and get my stuff taken down? Also, what do I actually get out of this and how long will it take?

facts.about: Her maiden name used before marriage
When she sent the deletion request
facts.truth: August 28, 2026, so 45 days from retrieval would run into mid-October for brokers that retrieved it that week
Tucson, Arizona, in a rented duplex since 2023
Phoenix, where she lived 2019 to 2023 in an apartment
An Aisha Grant, about 58, in Mesa, who is not her
Her mother, Ngozi Okafor, is listed in Phoenix; Aisha does not manage her mother's data
Dan Reyes, who has his own listings and should not be touched

unknowns: How many days a broker has to respond after retrieving the request
What the status labels like 'opted out' or 'exempt' mean for her case
Which brokers are required to register with the state
Whether a listing under a former name counts as the same request
